newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed lower on Wednesday, reversing an early gain on the back of Wall Street's Tuesday gain and firmer bonds after a surprise quarter point rise in British interest rates.
"The UK rate rise has stimulated fear of interest rate rises in other countries," said one dealer, adding the evaporation of an early Wall Street rally also deflated Dutch shares.

The AEX index closed 4.66 points down at 577.09, way back from the session high of 586.61 and making a two day fall of around 14 points. "I think people are aware that we're near the top and are happy to take profits," said another dealer.

Dealers had mistrusted the earlier bounce which they said was mainly technical after Tuesday's big fall. "Some people are now looking at the market and wondering if the big sell off so many people are talking about might be coming soon," said one.
He was referring to recent comments from Wall Street guru Elaine Garzarelli that U.S. shares could fall 15-25 percent after the November 5 presidential election.
"Personally I feel our market is looking pretty good -- inflation and interest rates look under control -- but if Wall Street drops by that sort of amount we have to go with it," said another dealer.

Food and drinks group BolsWessanen closed a guilder higher at 29.60 on much higher than usual turnover of 3.09 million shares, boosted by early speculation in Britain that Grand Met was angling for a takeover. Bols dipped from a session high of 31.10 guilders after it said it had no such indication.

Supermarkets leader Ahold closed 60 cents off at 99.90 guilders, largely unmoved by news that regional supermarkets chain De Boer Winkelbedrijven planned to merge with unlisted sector rival Unigro to create a grocery combine which would be ranked second to Ahold. De Boer surged 12.50 guilders to 106.80 on the news.
Financial groups came under fire following the surprise British rate move with ING down 1.40 guilders to 52.20 and ABN AMRO 1.20 guilders off at 95.80.

Chemicals group DSM finished 1.50 guilders higher at 163.00, recovering some of Tuesday's 5.10 guilder plunge on lower than expected third quarter earnings after a broker reiterated a buy recommendation on the belief the shares were undervalued.
Elsewhere Philps closed unchanged at 59.20 guilders and Royal Dutch, which reports third quarter results on Thursday, lost 90 cents to 286.00 -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
